properties.name: Precursor chemicals: China to Mexico's Pacific ports
properties.text: Fentanyl and methamphetamine precursors and pill-press parts ship mainly from China, increasingly also from India, to Mexico's Pacific ports such as Manzanillo and Lázaro Cárdenas.

properties.name: Precursor chemicals: India to Mexico
properties.text: Treasury sanctioned India-based chemical suppliers selling precursors to the Sinaloa Cartel in April 2026.

properties.name: Synthetic drugs: Sinaloa to Arizona and California crossings
properties.text: Fentanyl pressed in Sinaloa moves north through Sonora to the Nogales and other Arizona ports of entry, mostly in passenger and cargo vehicles.

properties.name: Synthetic drugs: Sinaloa and Jalisco to Baja California
properties.text: Synthetic drugs move up the Pacific corridor to San Ysidro, Otay Mesa and Calexico.

properties.name: Cocaine: Colombia's Pacific coast to Central America and Mexico
properties.text: Go-fast boats and semi-submersibles carry cocaine from Buenaventura and Tumaco north along the eastern Pacific. This is the zone of US boat strikes since September 2025.

properties.name: Cocaine: Ecuador's ports to Europe and North America
properties.text: Containerised cocaine leaves Guayaquil, often through the Panama Canal, to Europe and the US. Los Choneros and Los Lobos fight over the port economy.

properties.name: Cocaine: Caribbean route via Venezuela and Hispaniola
properties.text: Cocaine leaves from Venezuela's coast and from airstrips in Apure and Zulia toward the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Florida. US strikes have also hit boats in the Caribbean.

properties.name: Cocaine: Brazil and Southern Cone to Europe and Africa
properties.text: Bolivian and Peruvian cocaine reaches Santos and other Atlantic ports. The PCC controls much of this trade toward Europe and West Africa.

properties.name: Cocaine: Central American land bridge to Mexico
properties.text: Cocaine landed on the Honduran Mosquitia coast crosses Guatemala's Petén into Chiapas, then moves north to the Tamaulipas border.

properties.name: Human smuggling: Darién Gap to the US border
properties.text: The Clan del Golfo taxes migrant crossings from Necoclí through the Darién. Smuggling networks charge along the route to the US border.

properties.name: Firearms: US to Mexico (southbound)
properties.text: Most firearms recovered and traced in Mexico come from the United States, smuggled south through the same crossings.

properties.name: Bulk cash: US to Mexico (southbound)
properties.text: Drug proceeds return south as bulk cash. They increasingly go through Chinese money laundering networks instead, which buy dollars inside the US (see Money flows).
